newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-BENARBIA COMES OF AGE AS MONACO FLOURISH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BENARBIA COMES OF AGE AS MONACO FLOURISH.

text.p: A week ago, Ali Benarbia, was a long way from being a household name in European soccer.
Talk about his club Monaco and people would first mention players such as Anderson, Victor Ikpeba and John Collins as well as coach Jean Tigana.
But that all changed last Tuesday when his two goals helped sink English club Newcastle United 3-0 and set up a mouthwatering UEFA Cup semifinal with Italian giants Inter Milan.
And on the domestic front, Monaco also probably owe their position at the top of the French first division more to Benarbia than any other player.
A late developer, the 28-year-old Benarbia made his first division debut for Martigues only in 1993 before joining Monaco two years ago.

But he has developed into the latest in a line of gifted playmakers at the club, which includes current England coach Glenn Hoddle, and such is his form that Belgium's Enzo Scifo is struggling even to find a place on the bench.
Born in Oman, Algeria, the builder's son arrived in France at the age of eight months and is eligible to play for either country.
So far he has been overlooked by both although that could soon change.
"I'd love to contribute to the French team...but I get the impression Monaco are ignored," Benarbia said recently.
"The side at the top of the championship is only represented in the French team by two players often on the bench -- (goalkeeper Fabien) Barthez and (defender Patrick) Blondeau.
"When Marseille and Paris (St Germain) were at the top, they had five or six players (in the France team)."
That could change if Monaco lift their first league title since Hoddle inspired them in 1988. And heading the table by seven points with eight games to go, that looks increasingly likely.
"Qualifying for the final of the UEFA Cup and winning the championship will be the best response," said Benarbia who credits Tigana for much of the team's success.
"He's transmitted this will to win. And, better, he's transmitted it to the directors, too, and today we feel they're there when it matters."
Benarbia will not, however, be disappointed if he never gets the France call for he loves his football too much to worry.
"I take a real pleasure in finding my striker as quickly as possible and, above all, being able to put him in the best position so all he has to do is control the ball and put it in the net.
"I always want to progress and I always think I'm missing something and that I'll only have that understanding of the game by working hard at it," added Benarbia.
He is also wary of the commercial side of the game and points to the new Tom Cruise film "Jerry McGuire" as an example.
"That films emphasises a bit what's going on nowadays, with people thinking only about business and financial success...and it shows there can be other, healthier ways of getting there."
Benarbia is now hoping for an unbeatable double this year of a league championship winner's medal and the birth of a baby daughter in June.
"She may arrive with the title, which will help make 1997 an exceptional year for me."
